title: The Last Terminal Again
premise: Mirabel Hartwell discovers that the cryosleepers in his cargo hold are not colonists but a hidden second archive of humanity — and that one of them, a woman named Ilsa Vane, is listed as the ship's original navigator on a flight record that shouldn't exist. As rival factions converge to claim the sleepers, Mirabel learns he is himself a backup of a man who died fifteen years ago, and that waking half the sleepers will kill the other half through power constraints. In the end, Mirabel sacrifices his own continuity — letting his original's memory overwrite him — to wake everyone, trusting Ilsa to carry both their lives forward.
about_author: Sebastian Crane is the pen name of a former merchant marine radio officer who spent a decade writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. He lives in a coastal town where he restores vintage navigation instruments and claims he still dreams in dead reckoning.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomaly
chapters.summary: Mirabel, running routine cargo through contested orbits, finds an impossible name on his own ship's manifest: Ilsa Vane, navigator of a vessel that never flew. His POV establishes his loneliness and the low dread he feels near the sleeper hold. The emotional beat is quiet unease — a crack in fifteen years of numb routine.

chapters.title: The Hold That Breathes
chapters.summary: Mirabel breaks protocol and enters the cryo bay, finding three hundred sleepers with mismatched serial numbers and one pod already empty. Through his POV we learn the pods draw power in patterns too regular to be accidental. Emotional beat: fascination curdling into violation — someone has been using his ship as a cradle.

chapters.title: Ilsa
chapters.summary: The empty pod's occupant, Ilsa Vane, reveals herself living secretly aboard, awake for months. Her POV chapter shows her decoding the ship's logs and recognizing Mirabel's face from records dated after his supposed death. Emotional beat: wary connection between two people who are both lies on paper.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years Gone
chapters.summary: Ilsa shows Mirabel the truth: he is a backup copy of the original Hartwell, who died saving these sleepers from a corporate purge. His POV fractures under the revelation; memories he trusted feel staged. Emotional beat: grief for a self he never got to mourn, and rage at whoever made him without asking.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: A salvage fleet arrives claiming jurisdiction over the 'lost archive.' Mirabel stalls them with forged transponders while Ilsa works the old navigation codes only she knows. Alternating POVs build the chase. Emotional beat: duty versus love crystallizes — each realizes they'd trade the mission for the other.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Waking
chapters.summary: Ilsa decodes the archive: the ship can wake only half the sleepers; the rest die when power reroutes. Mirabel insists there must be another way; she runs the numbers until they bleed. Dual POV. Emotional beat: the horror of a solvable equation with no humane answer — survival priced in strangers.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Mirabel finds the original Hartwell's sealed message: a plan to merge his backup pattern with the ship's life-support AI, freeing enough power to wake everyone — at the cost of the copy's continuity. His POV. Emotional beat: understanding, then terror, then a terrible calm acceptance beginning to form.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Salvagers breach the hull; Ilsa fights to hold the bridge while Mirabel descends into the hold to begin the merge. Her POV carries the action — brutal, close-quarters, desperate. Emotional beat: love declared in the worst possible moment, shouted over decompression alarms.

chapters.title: The Last Terminal
chapters.summary: Climax. Mirabel initiates the merge as the original's memories flood in — fifteen lost years, the real Ilsa he loved and lost, the choice made twice now. He wakes all three hundred sleepers as his own pattern dissolves. His POV, fragmenting beautifully. Emotional beat: sacrifice as an act of love, not duty.

chapters.title: Both Our Names
chapters.summary: Resolution. Ilsa guides the crowded ship to sanctuary, the sleepers waking to a world that moved on. She carries Mirabel's merged memories — both versions of him alive inside her telling of things. Final beat: bittersweet hope; survival was paid for, but what remains chooses to remember generously.
